meta.summary: An agentic terminal harness: a native macOS app and a browser Workbench are clients of a per-user Rust daemon (axod) that owns PTYs, Pi agent processes and the session catalog; a Cloudflare Worker relays remote clients to linked hosts.
meta.coverage: First pass. Daemon (axo-server, axo-pty, axo-pi, axo-ipc, axo-relay, axo-protocol), API Worker and pi-axo read in depth; Mac app and web app read at the level of their RPC usage only.

actors.summary: Per-user daemon. Authoritative owner of Workspaces, Sessions and Panes, their PTYs and Pi processes, the SQLite catalog, and the local JSON-RPC API. Keeps running when the app quits.
SwiftUI macOS app. Registers axod as a LaunchAgent, renders panes with libghostty surfaces, and drives the catalog through local RPC. Holds no authoritative session state.
macOS service manager. Owns axod's process lifetime once registered through SMAppService.
The Pi agent CLI, an external program axod runs interactively in a PTY. Sole writer of its JSONL conversation file.

First-party Pi extension loaded inside each Pi process. Verifies Pi's session file, serves the per-session bridge socket, forwards structured events and executes commands from axod through Pi's public APIs.
The user's configured shell running in an axod-owned PTY.
Cloudflare Worker at axo.leostera.dev/api. OAuth sign-in, host pairing, and the relay between browser clients and linked hosts.
AxoAccountManager Durable Object, one per Axo account. Owns web sessions, pairings, host memberships and credential verifiers, and hosts the relay sockets for that account's hosts and clients.
Maps an OAuth (issuer, subject) to an immutable Axo account ID.
Short-lived index from a pairing code to its account, plus pairing rate limiting.
AxoSessionDO, one per (account, host, session). Durable server-side copy of structured Pi events.
Browser Workbench at /app. Lists hosts and sessions, drives remote terminals and shows Pi history.
Stores the host credential used by axod's relay connection.

messages.summary: Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0. Parameters reject unknown fields. Method names are declared once in a table and advertised by negotiation.
Attach protocol v2: client sends a shell ID; axod replies with a rejection code, or a replay length, the PTY master descriptor over SCM_RIGHTS, then replay followed by live output.
Newline-delimited JSON over a per-session Unix socket. axod connects and authenticates with the session's bridge token; Pi answers with its identity, then streams events and answers commands.
accepts: command: send / steer / follow-up / cancel / shutdownIfIdle

messages.summary: Relay JSON-RPC between hosts (daemon role) and browser clients (client role).
emits: host events: session.snapshot, session.removed, shell.activity, terminal.output, pi.event

messages.summary: Public HTTP routes. Account-scoped routes under /api/v1; legacy /v1 routes use synthetic edge principals.

flows.summary: axod opens its catalog, restores what was open, repairs session invariants, then starts accepting attachments and reaping exits.
flows.trigger: launchd starts axod

steps.action: open SQLite catalog (WAL, synchronous=FULL, foreign keys) and migrate schema to user_version 7 in one transaction
load or create host ID, agent.command, shell.command and last client viewport
generate a new host generation (per boot)
create the private pi-sessions directory (0700); remove abandoned Pi bridge sockets
restore Workspace directory access from stored security-scoped bookmarks
restore open sessions: respawn terminal panes; mark Pi panes unavailable
properties: terminal output history is not restored

steps.action: recover each unavailable Pi pane
create a session in every open Workspace that has none
create a standalone home session if none is open
listen on the attach socket (0600)
start the reaper thread

flows.summary: The Mac app ensures axod is registered with launchd and running the same build as the app.
flows.trigger: app launch or explicit user action

steps.action: resolve registration decision from SMAppService status and recorded intent
properties: registers only once automatically; user-disabled is respected

steps.action: register the bundled daemon as a per-user LaunchAgent
call axo.daemon.health
compare daemon build number to app build number; on mismatch ask launchd to restart the service from the current bundle

flows.summary: Create a Workspace for a project directory together with its first Pi-backed session.
flows.trigger: axo.workspace.create {name, directoryPath, directoryBookmark?}

steps.action: validate name and require an absolute directory path
open the directory with normal permissions, or resolve the security-scoped bookmark
insert Workspace row (state open)
create the first Workspace session
on session failure, mark the Workspace archived
hold directory access for as long as the Workspace is open
start the Pi bridge worker
publish session.snapshot and workspace.changed

flows.summary: Create a Session inside a Workspace with one Pi pane bound to a fresh, exact conversation file.
flows.trigger: axo.workspace.session.create, axo.remote.workspace.session.create, or invariant repair

steps.action: read the open Workspace's directory
allocate session UUID, pane UUID, Pi session file path (pi-sessions/<workspace>/<uuid>.jsonl) and bridge socket path
insert Session row, insert Pi shell row, write single-pane layout
properties: three separate statements, not one transaction

steps.action: spawn Pi in a PTY with --session <path> and the extension environment
properties: happens while holding the catalog mutex

steps.action: on spawn failure, archive the Session (reason pi_spawn_failed)
start pi-axo bridge server once Pi's actual session file matches the configured path
start the Pi bridge worker and publish session.snapshot

flows.summary: Create a Workspace-less terminal session rooted at $HOME.
flows.trigger: axo.session.create, axo.remote.session.create, or invariant repair

steps.action: insert Session row named 'Session N'
insert shell row and spawn the configured shell in a PTY sized for the current viewport
on spawn failure, archive shell and Session (reason spawn_failed)
publish session.snapshot

flows.summary: Add a terminal pane to a Session and persist the new layout.
flows.trigger: user split in the Mac app or browser

steps.action: call axo.shell.create
insert shell row and spawn shell in a PTY pre-sized from the stored viewport
call axo.session.layout.set with the new split tree
validate layout (binary tree, ≤64 depth, ≤255 nodes, leaves are this Session's open panes) and persist it
resize unattached panes to fit the layout; publish session.snapshot

flows.summary: Close a Session; replace it first if it was the last of its kind.
flows.trigger: axo.session.close or axo.remote.session.close; also closing a Pi pane or a Session's last pane

steps.action: if it is the last open Session in its Workspace, create a replacement Workspace session
if it is the last open standalone Session, create a replacement home session
archive the Session (reason explicit_close) and drop its Pi activity
stop its processes on a background thread, outside the catalog mutex
properties: shell grace 500 ms, Pi grace 3 s, then kill

steps.action: start the replacement's Pi bridge, publish events

flows.summary: Every 100 ms, detect exited children and update the catalog.
flows.trigger: reaper tick (100 ms)

steps.action: try_wait every running child under the catalog mutex
properties: a child whose wait fails is not assumed exited, to avoid signalling a reused PID

steps.action: exited Pi pane: mark it unavailable; Session stays open
exited terminal pane: archive shell and prune layout in one transaction
Session with no remaining panes: archive it (reason shell_exited)
publish shell.activity exited, session.removed, session.snapshot
repair invariants: Workspace sessions and the home session

flows.summary: A client attaches to a pane: it receives replay, then live output, plus the PTY descriptor for input and resize.
flows.trigger: axod terminal-attach --shell-id (spawned per Ghostty surface by the Mac app)

steps.action: connect to attach socket, send shell ID (3 s request timeout)
acquire an attachment permit (max 256); otherwise reject DaemonBusy
subscribe to the pane's output pump atomically with reading its replay history (≤8 MiB)
send replay length, PTY master fd via SCM_RIGHTS, replay, then live output
publish shell.activity attached on first attachment, detached on last
disconnect a client that falls 8 MiB behind; it must reattach and replay

flows.summary: Write input bytes to a pane over RPC (used by remote clients) with exactly-once, in-order semantics per pane.
flows.trigger: axo.terminal.input or axo.remote.terminal.input {sessionId, shellId, sequence, data}

steps.action: decode base64; require 1 to 49,152 bytes
acknowledge and ignore a repeated sequence; reject a gap
write to the PTY master with a 5 s timeout

flows.summary: Clients long-poll for catalog and stream events through bounded per-subscription queues.
flows.trigger: axo.session.subscribe, then repeated axo.session.events.next

steps.action: expire subscriptions not polled for 60 s; reject beyond 64 subscriptions
create a 128-event queue in catalog or streams scope, optionally for one session
queue current session snapshots for this subscriber only
long-poll: wait up to timeoutMs (1 to 20,000), return up to maxEvents (1 to 256)
properties: waiting polls are futures, not threads

steps.action: on overflow, replace the backlog with a single subscription.lagged marker; client resynchronizes from a fresh list

flows.summary: axod follows the running Pi over its bridge socket, turning Pi events into catalog state and relayable events.
flows.trigger: Pi pane started or recovered

steps.action: connect to the Pi's bridge socket, retrying every 100 ms while the pane is current
authenticate with the session's bridge token
reply with identity: Pi session ID, exact file path, Axo session and pane IDs, process ID
bind only if every identity field matches the launched pane; otherwise reject the connection
persist Pi session ID
stream events with strictly increasing sequence (≤60,000 bytes of data each)
update activity: working on agent.start, idle on agent.settled, needs-attention while UI prompts are open
write Pi-chosen title and emoji to the Session row
publish pi.event (opaque payload) and session.snapshot when state changed

flows.summary: Restart an unavailable Pi pane against its exact existing conversation, taking the transcript over from any Pi still holding it.
flows.trigger: daemon startup, axo.session.pi.restart.auto.v1 (app auto-restart), or axo.session.pi.restart.force.v2 (explicit user restart)

steps.action: under the catalog mutex: check pane is unavailable and not already recovering; reserve a recovery ID
require the Pi session file to be owned by exactly one Session row
outside the mutex: verify the history file exists and is Axo-owned (device/inode identity)
take over the transcript writer lock (flock)
properties: auto: ask Pi to shut down if idle, never force
force: escalate to signals aimed only at the verified Pi process group

steps.action: verify the history file did not change while waiting
briefly re-take the mutex: confirm reservation is current, rotate the bridge token
spawn Pi outside the mutex, inheriting the writer lock
commit only if the reservation is still current; otherwise stop the new child outside the mutex
start the Pi bridge worker, publish session.snapshot

flows.summary: Pi's /resume switches to another conversation; axod reopens the Session that owns it and closes the requester.
flows.trigger: pi-axo session.resume.requested (from session_before_switch)

steps.action: request resume with the target session file
validate path (non-empty, ≤4096 bytes, no NUL), canonicalize, require it inside pi-sessions and a regular file
reject if the requesting pane is stale
reopen the archived owning Session and its Workspace in one transaction; spawn its panes
in one catalog transition: require target Pi pane available, close requester Session
publish session.removed, session.focus (pending focus lives 10 s), session.snapshot

flows.summary: Cloudflare OAuth Authorization Code + PKCE sign-in that yields an Axo web session cookie.
flows.trigger: GET /api/auth/cloudflare/start

steps.action: create state and PKCE verifier in a sealed __Host-axo_oauth cookie (10 min)
redirect to Cloudflare authorization
on callback: verify state, exchange code, fetch userinfo
map (issuer, subject) to an immutable Axo account ID
store session digest, expiry and profile (transaction)
set __Host-axo_session cookie (30 days, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax); redirect to /app

flows.summary: Link a Mac to an account with a one-time 8-character code; the host gets its own revocable credential.
flows.trigger: user chooses Link a Mac on the web, then Link this Mac in Settings → Remote Access

steps.action: create pairing code (Crockford Base32, XXXX-YYYY, 10 min, ≤20 issued per minute) and store its verifier
index code → account
accept typed/pasted code or axo://pair/<code>; call axo.relay.link
validate code, generate a 32-byte host credential, store it in Keychain, persist credential ID and host generation in relay.json
POST redemption with host metadata and credential verifier over TLS (10 s timeout)
rate limit redemptions (120/min, 8/min per source)
atomically consume the code and upsert host membership (≤16 active hosts)
properties: repeating an identical redemption is idempotent

steps.action: if this replaced a host's credential, close that host's existing relay
connect the relay

flows.summary: axod keeps an authenticated outbound WebSocket to its account so remote clients can see and drive its sessions.
flows.trigger: relay configured/linked, daemon start, or axo.relay.connect

steps.action: open WSS with the host credential (5 s connect timeout, ≤5 redirects)
authorize: account matches, host not revoked, credential verifier matches
register host with remote session snapshots (Pi panes and paths removed)
subscribe to local events including streams
loop: heartbeat every 10 s; forward at most one local event; read one incoming frame with a 20 ms read timeout
renew route lease (30 s) on register and heartbeat
on subscription.lagged, resend current snapshots
on error, reconnect with backoff up to 30 s

flows.summary: A browser client drives a host: create/close sessions and shells, set layout, send input, resize.
flows.trigger: web-app sends axo.remote.* over its client WebSocket

steps.action: connect client WebSocket with the Axo session cookie
record a pending correlation (≤32 per client, ≤128 per host, 10 s deadline)
forward the call to the host's socket
execute against the local catalog
reply over the relay
match reply to pending entry, deliver to client

flows.summary: Structured Pi events are copied to a per-session Durable Object and paged by the browser.
flows.trigger: pi.event forwarded by the relay; browser GET .../sessions/:session/events

steps.action: forward pi.event with sequence and opaque payload
store via AxoSessionDO named (account, host, session)
page events after a cursor (1 to 50 per page)
check ownership binding, return page

flows.summary: An account owner unlinks a host.
flows.trigger: POST /api/v1/account/hosts/:host/revoke

steps.action: set revoked_at on the host
close the host's relay socket; future connections fail authorization
retain last-known metadata as offline

state.summary: SQLite at ~/.axo/server/axo.db (0600): workspaces, sessions, shells, daemon_metadata (host ID, configured commands, viewport, bridge tokens). Rows are archived with a reason, not deleted.

SessionState behind one mutex: running panes (child, PTY master, output pump, last input sequence), unavailable Pi panes and recovery reservations, Pi activity, configured commands, viewport. Also guards the database connection.
Per-pane in-memory replay buffer of VT output, up to 8 MiB. If exceeded, replay is skipped rather than partial.
Pi's canonical JSONL conversation at ~/.axo/server/pi-sessions/<workspace>/<session-uuid>.jsonl, with a sibling .lock file held by flock while Pi runs.
relay.json (≤16 KiB): relay URL, account routing ID, credential ID, pairing-time host generation. The credential itself lives in Keychain.
Registry of local subscriptions and their bounded queues.
state.lifetime: process; idle subscriptions expire after 60 s

state.summary: Per-account SQLite: web sessions (digest only), pairings (verifier only), account_hosts (credential verifier, generation, revoked_at), host session snapshots, relay routes and pending correlations.
Server-side copy of structured Pi events per (account, host, session). A projection; not the canonical transcript.
AxoHostDirectory for legacy/unassigned (private-fleet) hosts on /v1 routes.
TerminalSessionsModel: a client-side projection of daemon sessions, plus selected session (UserDefaults) and pending local layouts.

stateMachines.summary: A pane is available, or unavailable with a non-empty reason; the wire form enforces the pairing.
Bridge connection authenticates, then binds to the exact pane, then carries one increasing event stream. Anything else rejects the connection.
Relay status reported to local clients.

boundaries.summary: JSON-RPC params are deserialized into typed structs that reject unknown fields; requests are capped at 8 MiB and 64 in flight per connection.
Name validated, path must be absolute, directory opened (or bookmark resolved) before any row is written.
LayoutNode arrives structurally typed; the handler validates depth, size and pane membership before persisting.
Base64 decoded and size-checked before the PTY write.

agent.command and shell.command are parsed with shell-style quoting (no shell invoked), ≤4096 bytes and ≤128 arguments; executables resolved against PATH or required absolute; managed Pi flags rejected.
Records ≤8 MiB parsed into typed Record; connection state machine rejects identity mismatch, out-of-order sequence, oversize names/data.
A path supplied by Pi is canonicalized and confined to the pi-sessions directory before lookup.
Client viewport bounded (area, scale, cell size, padding, ratios) before grid sizes are computed.
Worker and Durable Objects parse requests with zod schemas from @axo/protocol (frame ≤64 KiB, ≤8 batched calls).
State, PKCE verifier, fixed callback URI and allowlisted return destination validated; identity is the verified subject, never email.
URLs from terminal output are treated as untrusted before opening.

invariants.statement: At least one standalone (Workspace-less) Session rooted at $HOME is open.
enforcedBy: runtime repair at startup, on close and after reaping
invariants.consequence: The app would have no default terminal to show.

invariants.statement: Every open Workspace has at least one open Session.
enforcedBy: runtime repair at startup, on close and after reaping
invariants.consequence: An open Workspace with nothing to show.

invariants.statement: A Workspace Session has exactly one Pi pane; closing it closes the Session. Closing the last pane closes the Session.
Only the output pump reads a PTY master; attached clients get the descriptor for input, resize and termios only.
invariants.consequence: A client reading the fd would steal output from other clients and history.

invariants.statement: A shell never blocks on a full PTY buffer because a client is slow or absent; slow clients are disconnected at 8 MiB backlog.
A subscriber's replay plus its live chunks are exactly the PTY stream: no gap, no duplicate.
Only Pi writes its JSONL transcript; axod never writes or creates it.
Holding the transcript flock proves no Pi for that Session is alive; only acquire() can produce a WriterLock.
A Pi transcript file is referenced by exactly one Session; recovery never chooses 'most recent' and never creates a new transcript at an old path.
Pi takeover waits and child termination happen outside the catalog mutex.
invariants.consequence: Every client stalls while the mutex is held.

invariants.statement: The RPC executor never blocks: synchronous handlers run on the blocking pool, long-polls are futures.
Publishers never block; a full subscriber queue is replaced by a single lagged marker rather than presenting a silent gap.
Per pane, RPC input sequences start at zero and are consecutive; a repeat is acknowledged and ignored.
Every spawned child is a session leader on its PTY and inherits only its PTY and explicitly listed descriptors.
A host credential is valid for exactly one host, is stored only as a verifier server-side, and is revoked by unlinking that host.
Authorization derives from validated credentials and account ownership, never from a caller-selected role, host ID or email. Account routes never fall back to legacy principals.

contracts.summary: Protocol version 1, negotiated; method list advertised. Versioned method names (…restart.force.v2, …restart.auto.v1) carry behaviour changes.
JSON Schemas under schemas/axo.leostera.dev/v1 with fixtures; Rust types are checked for conformance.
Shared between Rust and the TypeScript extension.
SQLite user_version 7, with in-place migrations (legacy_sessions rename, added layout and workspace columns).
Compatibility layer: /v1/* routes with synthetic edge principals and the unassigned private-fleet directory coexist with account-scoped /api/v1/*. No removal condition stated in code.

observability.summary: key=value log events (event=session.*, relay.*) with session/shell/runtime IDs and error kinds.
Waits for and holds of the catalog mutex over 50 ms are logged.
RPC requests slower than 100 ms are reported.
No trace context observed crossing the Mac ↔ axod ↔ relay ↔ Worker boundaries; flows are followed by IDs in logs.
axod-loadtest drives the daemon and reports metrics/stats.

measurements.subject: RPC request size / in flight per connection
relay heartbeat / lease / max reconnect delay
relay pending calls
measurements.value: 32 per client, 128 per host, 10 s deadline

measurements.subject: hosts per account / clients per host

claims.statement: Shells keep running and producing output when no client is attached.
Long-polling for events never delays unrelated requests.
Open tabs and shells are restored after a daemon restart, but terminal screen contents are not.
New panes start at the latest client's viewport size, even across restarts.
A daemon restart restores each Pi conversation against its own exact transcript and never replays prompts or shell input.
Automatic Pi recovery never forcibly stops a running Pi; only an explicit user restart may signal it.
The daemon keeps running when the menu-bar app quits, and is restarted when its build differs from the app's.
Cloudflare OAuth tokens are never given to axod or browser JavaScript.
Terminal bytes never cross the host boundary.
claims.note: RFD0014 (Proposal) states this, but the relay subscribes with streams and forwards terminal.output to the account Durable Object so the browser Workbench can show remote terminals. RFD0013's narrower statement, that terminal bytes are not persisted in account storage, was not contradicted in this pass.

claims.statement: Project paths stay on the host; remote snapshots omit Pi panes and paths.

The relay forwards at most one local event per loop iteration, and each iteration may wait up to 20 ms for an incoming frame, so with a quiet cloud side forwarding is bounded near 50 events per second; bursts of terminal output will lag the 128-event queue and fall back to snapshot resync.
A single PTY read larger than roughly 48 KiB becomes a terminal.output frame above the 65,536-byte relay limit; send_json rejects it and the relay session ends and reconnects.
claims.note: PTY reads up to 64 KiB; base64 adds a third. The input direction is capped at 49,152 bytes for exactly this reason, but no output chunking was found.

claims.statement: Process spawning and PTY input writes happen while holding the single catalog mutex, so a slow spawn or a blocked PTY write (up to 5 s) stalls every other catalog operation.
Creating a Workspace and its first Session is one logical operation.
claims.note: RFD0014 describes it as one logical operation. In code it is several separate writes with a compensating archive on failure, not a database transaction; a crash between writes would leave a Workspace without a Session, which startup repair then fills.

claims.statement: A linked host can call the full current protocol; there are no per-method or per-session capability restrictions in v1.
